candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — legal responsibilities, advocacy and workplace safety
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — protected workplace-safety reporting
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize federal anti-retaliation protection for employees who engage in protected workplace-safety reporting under OSH Act Section 11(c).

options.A: Section 11(c) of the OSH Act prohibits retaliation for protected workplace-safety activities such as raising safety concerns or filing an OSHA complaint, and a worker who experiences retaliation should contact OSHA promptly
options.B: Employers may discipline workers solely for filing a workplace-safety complaint because reporting hazards is not a protected activity
options.C: OSHA whistleblower protections guarantee a promotion or financial reward whenever a worker reports a hazard
options.D: Section 11(c) protects only physicians and does not apply to other covered employees such as nurses

candidate.rationale: OSHA states that Section 11(c) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act prohibits retaliation against employees for exercising protected workplace-safety rights, including raising safety concerns with an employer, filing a safety and health complaint with OSHA, participating in an OSHA inspection, or reporting a work-related injury or illness. A worker who believes retaliation occurred should contact OSHA promptly because filing deadlines apply. Protection does not guarantee a reward or immunity from legitimate nonretaliatory employment actions.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Covered employees are protected from employer retaliation for specified workplace-safety activities under OSH Act Section 11(c); retaliation complaints are subject to filing requirements.
candidate.source_document_title: Worker Participation; OSHA Online Whistleblower Complaint Form
candidate.source_locator: Worker Participation: Section 11(c) prohibits retaliation for filing an OSHA safety complaint, raising safety concerns, participating in an inspection, or reporting work-related injury/illness; whistleblower complaint information explains adverse action and filing requirements
candidate.stem: A nurse reports a recurring workplace safety hazard to the employer and then files a safety complaint with OSHA. The nurse is later threatened with discipline specifically because of the report. Which statement is most accurate?
